newsitem.title: JAPAN: SWIMMING-HEYNS-RILEY CLASH TO TOP PAN PACIFIC MEET.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-HEYNS-RILEY CLASH TO TOP PAN PACIFIC MEET.

text.p: An expected battle between South Africa's double Olympic champion Penny Heyns and Samantha Riley of Australia should be one of the highlights of the Pan Pacific Swimming Championships which start on Sunday.
"I think it'll be very exciting to watch," veteran Australian head coach Don Talbot said of the anticipated clashes between Heyns and Riley in the 100 metre and 200 metre breastroke races.
"That'll be a great, hard battle," said South African head coach Alisdair Hatfield.
He said Heyns was back in form after missing the world short-course championships in Sweden in April because extra demands on her time after the Olympics cut into her training.
Riley and Heynes are among the approximately 300 swimmers from 23 countries and regions competing in the championships being held at Fukuoka on the southern Japanese island of Kyushu.
The event has been shortened to four days after a typhoon caused the the 25-km open water race to be put back by one day.

Other highlights will include the appearance of Brooke Bennett, a gold medalist in Atlanta in the 800 freestyle and considered the successor to U.S. swimming queen Janet Evans, especially after capturing three gold in the recently completed U.S. nationals.
"Brooke Bennett is someone we think will be hard to beat in anything over 400 and will give Claudia Poll a race in the 400," said head U.S. women's coach John Collins.
Poll, Costa Rica's Olympic champion in the 200 freestyle, smashed her own world record in the 200 at the world short-course championships in April.
Australia's Talbot said he had to leave several swimmers at home because of a flu bug which hit his team.

They include Natasha Bowron, who won the 800 freestyle at the short-course championships and would have been a possible challenger to Bennett. But Talbot still has plenty of talent and experience in his squad, including Susan O'Neill, gold medalist in the 200 butterfly at Atlanta, and Grant Hackett "who will do very well in the 1,500", Talbot said.
Other top swimmers include Americans Tom Dolan, gold medalist at Atlanta in the 400 individual medley, and Brad Bridgewater, who took the 200 backstroke gold at the Olympics.

The Chinese have included in their team double Olympic gold medalist Le Jingyi, who will race in the women's 50 and 100 freestyle, and Cai Huijie, who set a world best time in the 50 butterfly in May in Monaco.
